rv.q: More than anything, Andrew Panton’s production for Dundee Rep and the National Theatre of Scotland is one big, happy laugh.
With its niche in-jokes and playfully deranged musical numbers, it’s the perfect tonic to the constant barrage of bad news to which we’re all exposed on a daily basis.
Nonetheless, The High Life:The Musical is a hilarious, camp and fun production which soars from take off until landing, transporting passengers both old and new on a fun ride through sunny skies.

The end result in Andrew Panton’s production - presented by the National Theatre of Scotland and Dundee Rep Theatre in association with Aberdeen Performing Arts and Capital Theatres - is a gloriously knowing confection writ large on Colin Richmond’s ever expanding jet age set.
Cumming and Masson let us join them in this celebration of a Scottish underdog flying high.

cn.t: Critics hail this musical adaptation of the cult '90s sitcom as a deliriously silly triumph, packed with fourth-wall-breaking gags and crowd-pleasing references that capture the show's exquisitely ridiculous spirit.
